findings.body: At $12.50, it is $6 above the $6.50 peer median and the highest of the 10 peers that publish it (middle half of the market: $5–$10). Customers who enroll in overdraft protection are doing what you ask; a premium transfer fee works against that.

findings.headline: Smaller premiums elsewhere on the schedule.
findings.body: Your outgoing domestic wire fee ($30 vs a $25 median, n=10) and your outgoing international wire fee ($60 vs a $40 median, n=9) also sit above the peer 75th percentile. Individually modest, together they shape how the schedule reads in a side-by-side comparison.

findings.stat_label: comparable lines inside the market range
findings.headline: Most of your schedule is priced with the market.
findings.body: Of the 7 fee lines where we found both your published amount and at least eight comparable peers, four sit between the peer 25th and 75th percentiles, three above.

exec_narrative: Burke & Herbert Bank & Trust Company is compared with 68 banks of similar size nationwide that publish fee schedules in the Bank Fee Index; a national set is used because fewer than 15 same-size peers in Virginia have published data, so local competitors may price differently. Of 7 rankable lines, four sit inside the middle half of the market, three above it (overdraft-protection transfer fee, outgoing domestic wire fee and outgoing international wire fee). We would suggest one step: review the overdraft-protection transfer fee, which sits above the market range; the peer median of $6.50 is the reference point.

callouts.title: Overdraft-protection transfer fee — $12.50
callouts.stat: Peer median $6.50 · middle half $5–$10 · range $5–$10 · 100th percentile · n=10
callouts.body: Published as “Overdraft Protection Transfer Fee.” At $12.50 it is $6 above the $6.50 peer median. Customers who enroll in overdraft protection are doing what you ask; a premium transfer fee works against that. A penalty fee offers little service to differentiate on, so the peer median of $6.50 is the natural reference point.

callouts.title: Outgoing domestic wire fee — $30
callouts.stat: Peer median $25 · middle half $21.25–$28.75 · range $15–$35 · 80th percentile · n=10
callouts.body: Published as “Outgoing Domestic Wire.” At $30 it is $5 above the $25 peer median. Wire fees fall mostly on business and higher-balance customers, the relationships most likely to compare institutions. Holding the premium is reasonable if the service behind it is differentiated; otherwise the peer median of $25 is the reference point.

callouts.title: Outgoing international wire fee — $60
callouts.stat: Peer median $40 · middle half $36–$50 · range $30–$50 · 100th percentile · n=9
callouts.body: Published as “Outgoing International Wire.” At $60 it is $20 above the $40 peer median. Volumes are typically low; the premium matters mainly to the few customers who use the service. Holding the premium is reasonable if the service behind it is differentiated; otherwise the peer median of $40 is the reference point.

context_narrative:
Overdraft and returned-item fees have been the focus of regulatory and public attention since 2022, and many of the largest banks have reduced overdraft fees or eliminated NSF fees outright. Community institutions have moved more slowly and more unevenly, which is why the spread inside a peer set is often wider than the headline national averages suggest.

Fee schedules are also now public in a practical sense: they are collected, compared and summarized automatically. A customer or examiner comparing Burke & Herbert Bank & Trust Company with its peers sees the same published lines this report uses, so the schedule is a positioning document as much as a pricing one.

How to use this report: § 02 shows every line against the peer range; § 03 explains the lines that sit outside it; § 05 names peers line by line. Ranked comparisons require at least eight peers publishing the same line. Where your institution offers several amounts for one category, the report uses the standard consumer charge described in the methodology below.
